answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token before it may submit jobs or vote on disputes. If identities are later linked by evidence of duplicate control, the protocol slashes the locked stake and distributes part to reporters. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for every identity, while risking forfeiture. A ripple of linked accounts can expose a comet-sized cluster in the atlas of transactions, but detection alone is not proof; slashing needs a defined challenge process to limit false accusations.
